messages:
maria_support: FYI escalation from AcmePay — they report a big jump in tail latency on /v1/generate (us-west-2) starting ~2026-01-24T14:22Z. p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.6s, p99 to ~3.8s. They say it started after a campaign spike but only affects their tenant. Request sample and logs below.

maria_support: sample curl they sent:
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1.1","input":"summarize: long doc","max_tokens":512}' -w '\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} TIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n'

maria_support: Their client-side time_total avg: 1.8s, server responded 200. No 5xx. Only expensive tail.

alert-bot: [LATENCY] us-west-2 /v1/generate p99 > 3s for tenant acmepay (alertid: LTN-2026-01124) — firing at 2026-01-24T14:23:10Z. Graph: https://grafana/reports/ltc-acmepay

lee_sre: @maria_support thanks. Do we have request traces? need route, model variant, queued time and exec time. Also confirm no infra deploys in the last 6h.

maria_support: Attaching their trace snippet (sanitized): 
```
trace_id=tr_01F.. tenant=acmepay route=/v1/generate model=redwood-xl-1.1 variant=fp16 region=us-west-2
recv_time=0.002s queue_time=0.450s exec_time=1.200s stream_flush=0.100s total=1.752s
```

maria_support: They said traffic spike ~200rps baseline -> 1.5k rps for 2 minutes. Only their tenant had big spikes.

devin_runtime: Queue_time 450ms is the problem — batching/backpressure. Likely continuous batching accumulation and busy GPUs. Are the autoscalers hitting max pods? 

lee_sre: Checking infra: no recent deploys. Autoscaler metrics show pod_count steady at 18 -> hit max 18 for that nodepool at 14:21:30Z. GPU utilization 92% on that pool.

jordan_se: Suggest short-term mitigation: divert acmepay to a lower-latency routing policy (smaller model / dedicated pool) or enable per-tenant burst capacity. Can we toggle fallback model?

devin_runtime: We can enable per-tenant fallback to redwood-medium-quant which is ~2-3x faster per token. Quick config change: 
```
# enable tenant fallback in routing service
curl -X POST https://internal-config/routing/tenants/acmepay -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL' -d '{"fallback":"redwood-medium-quant","max_rate":15}'
```
I can push this as a hotfix if SRE OK.

lee_sre: Hotfix path approved. Also adding circuit-breaker to protect the cluster: if queue_time > 300ms for p95 for a tenant, apply max_concurrency=8 and route excess to fallback. Dev-runbook pls.

anika_prod: For product note — we should avoid hard-coding fallbacks per tenant long-term. Add a guardrail: default fallback + auto-routing to dedicated for enterprise when sustained p95>500ms for 2m. Also we should add an SLO alert that triggers an automated fallback policy before paging humans.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: routing-config v2026.01.24-hotfix -> 3/3 canary pods healthy; proceeding.

devin_runtime: Applied fallback for acmepay. Immediate effect: their p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 420ms within 30s. p99 reduced to ~900ms.

maria_support: AcmePay reports improved UX. They accepted temporary fallback. But they want root cause and permanent fix.

lee_sre: Root cause summary draft: sudden burst from customer saturated existing shared GPU pool; autoscaler hit max configured nodes; continuous batching increased queue times; our routing lacked early tenant-level circuit-breaker so one tenant could monopolize batching windows.

devin_runtime: Long-term mitigations I'm proposing:
- Add tenant-level token rate-limits + per-tenant max_concurrency.
- Implement circuit-breaker that triggers fallback model or dedicated routing when p95>300ms sustained 2m.
- Autoscaler: add fast-path scale-up for short spikes (burst capacity) and preemptive spin-up when in-pipeline queue > threshold.
- Batching tuning: lower max_batch_wait_ms for latency-sensitive tenants (5ms instead of 25ms) and cap max_batch_size for them.

anika_prod: And SLO guardrails: define product-level thresholds for enterprise tenants: p95 < 500ms, p99 < 2s under baseline traffic. If SLO breached for X% of last 5m, trigger automatic fallback + page on-call. Also create an error-budget policy that gates feature flags for big campaigns.

lee_sre: Operational playbook (short):
1) Immediate: enable tenant fallback (done).
2) Short-term (30m): carve out dedicated pool for acmepay if they want it; remove them from shared autoscaling group.
3) 4-24h: implement and roll out circuit-breaker + tenant rate limit config; update docs and runbook.
4) Postmortem: add metrics to dashboard: per-tenant queued_time histogram, per-tenant batch_size distribution.

jordan_se: For carving dedicated pool, steps: raise support ticket to sales->infra reservations; infra to create dedicated capacity pool and update tenant routing. Devin, can you open infra PR for nodepool resize?

devin_runtime: Will open PR. Quick commands for ops if needed now:
```
# temporarily reduce batch wait window for latency class
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-batching -p '{"data":{"latency_class.batch_wait_ms":"5"}}'
helm upgrade runtime ./charts/runtime -f values-prod.yaml
```

maria_support: Customer asked what guardrail prevents recurrence for other tenants. Can we add per-tenant soft quotas + immediate fallback policy?

lee_sre: Yes — implement soft quotas first (rate-limit responses with 429 w/ retry-after header) and concurrently a non-throttling fallback (route to smaller model). Soft quota will protect other tenants.

anika_prod: Also push the product change: allow enterprise customers to opt-in to 'latency-guarantee' plan that reserves capacity and enforces stricter SLOs and billing adjustments.

devin_runtime: Action items assigned:
- lee_sre: implement circuit-breaker config and paging thresholds (ETA 6h).
- devin_runtime: infra PR for burst nodepool + helm change to batching defaults (ETA 3h).
- jordan_se: coordinate dedicated capacity post-sales (ETA 24h).
- maria_support: follow-up with AcmePay and get final acceptance.

maria_support: I'll confirm with AcmePay and close escalation once they sign off. Thx all. :thumbsup:

lee_sre: I'll draft the short postmortem and add SLO guardrail todos. Will follow up in #postmortems.

deploy-bot: routing-config v2026.01.24-hotfix deployed to prod at 2026-01-24T14:28:45Z

maria_support: Closing loop — AcmePay confirmed perf stable for next 45m after fallback, will monitor. We'll keep this thread for the postmortem notes.
